Subject: Onramp briefing — PulseWare pilot scope, success criteria & access roadmap

Hi Jared / Aditi —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick write-up to capture what we agreed and the proposed next steps for the pilot (so we all have the same expectations). Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Highlights / pain points you shared
- Latency spikes on peak hours causing poor UX for live assistant (25% of requests see >500ms).
- Cost unpredictability: bursty token usage and lack of transparent per-endpoint unit economics.
- Compliance: data residency + KMS integration for customer-managed keys.

Pilot scope (proposed)
- Duration: 3 weeks of active evaluation + 1 week buffer for acceptance testing.
- Workloads: 1) Chat endpoint (real-time, 99th pctl latency target) 2) Batch embeddings (nightly processing).
- Volume: up to ~50k tokens/month for active testing; sample batches for embeddings (10k texts).
- Models to evaluate: open baseline (gpt-open-x) vs. quantized variant we run in dedicated pool.

Success criteria / acceptance tests
- Latency: 99th percentile < 250ms on chat under expected load (as measured by our trace harness).
- Cost: demonstrable ~30–40% reduction in estimated per-token cost vs your current baseline using Redwood batching + KV caching.
- Quality: no more than a 5% delta in prompt-eval pass-rate on your 120-sample prompt set (we will run paired A/B evals).

Owners & timeline
- PulseWare: provide sample prompts, representative traffic profile, and S3 access for sample data by Sep 6. (Owner: Jared)
- Redwood: configure dedicated environment, run prompt-evals, and provide weekly short readouts. (Owner: Mateo + Ben)
- Security checks: Irene will run initial compliance checklist and provide SOC2 evidence request template.

Access / setup checklist (what we need from you)
1) AWS IAM role or temporary creds scoped to an S3 bucket with sample objects.
2) IP allowlist for the dedicated pool OR VPC peering details if you prefer private connectivity.
3) A short label file describing prompt types and which are high-risk (PII).

Attachments referenced:
- SOW draft (SOW-draft-PulseWare.pdf) — preliminary, for scope confirmation.
- Prompt eval template (pulseware-prompt-eval-suite.csv) — please populate the sample labels.

Proposed next step: kickoff session to hand off access and map the evaluation plan. I have availability next week (Sep 7–10). Can we tentatively schedule a 60-minute kickoff on Thu, Sep 9 at 10:00 AM PT?

If that works, I will loop in our infra lead (Ben) and security (Irene) and share a short runbook before the meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
